headline: Price survives two match darts to beat Springer 16-15
standfirst: Gerwyn Price let a 7-3 lead slip, then broke Niko Springer’s throw in the decider to reach a Grand Slam semi-final against Kevin Doets.
body: Gerwyn Price survived two missed match darts from Niko Springer to win their Grand Slam of Darts quarter-final 16-15 in Wolverhampton on Friday, breaking throw in the 31st and final leg. The world No 4 had led 7-3 and 13-9, and still needed a 143 finish and a break in the decider to reach the last four.

The match turned in the run-in. Price was four clear at 13-9, but Springer, ranked 34th, won six of the next seven legs to lead 15-14 for the first time. Price answered with a 143 checkout to level, then took the decider in 14 darts, finishing on 78, even though Springer had the throw. Springer missed two darts at the winning double before Price stepped in.

Price had the more convincing first half: he won the opening two legs, including a 136 finish in leg two, and made six breaks of throw over the match to Springer’s five. Springer’s longest run was only three legs, but it was three at the right moment.

Springer averages 91.85 over the last 12 months against Price’s 98.67, yet for long spells he matched him. It is a painful way for the German to leave his best run at the event, having reached the last 16 in 2025.

For Price, whose best result here remains his 2018 win, the reward is a guaranteed £60,000 and a semi-final against Doets on Sunday at 1:15pm. Springer takes home £35,000. The two had met only once before, at the Czech Darts Open in September 2025, which Price won 6-2.
